gap: No result ChatGPT got quotes EG4's own 18kPV manual (v2.0.2) on running with no battery: it says to enable 'PV Grid Off' or 'No Battery' so solar can 'supply load when the grid fails', and it warns that 'the Off-Grid energy is supplied by solar and is not stable'. None of them mention that Sun Gold Power's SPH6548P, an off-grid UL 1741 unit, 'supports battery-free' operation either.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited Enphase briefs (iq8-grid and sunlight-backup-installation-guidelines) and the uncited top result outagemath.com/guides/solar-without-battery-power-outage. Outagemath already covers the 2-second shutdown rule in IEEE 1547, Enphase's limit of 30% of array output for backup loads, and the name of EG4's 'PV Grid Off' setting. It lists EG4's batteryless output as 'Not published' and does not give EG4's own warning that this mode is 'not stable'. None of the result pages I could read mention the Sun Gold Power SPH6548P. I couldn't extract text from the two cited Enphase PDFs or the cited Sol-Ark guides on device.report, so I couldn't check what they say.
decides: This confirms there are two ways to get batteryless backup and that both run only while the sun covers the load in real time. Enphase IQ8 Sunlight Backup is the only route where the maker publishes a sizing rule (loads at or below 30% of the IQ8 array's AC rating) and an automatic restart. The EG4 18kPV can power loads from PV alone during an outage, but EG4's manual says that power is unstable. That makes the EG4 a 'battery later' pick, not a dependable batteryless backup. The SPH6548P, which Dealectric lists at $1,035, runs without a battery, but its UL 1741 listing is for off-grid systems. It suits a shopper who wants appliances run directly from solar, not one who wants to send power back to the grid.
candidates: Enphase IQ8 Microinverters + IQ System Controller 2 + IQ Load Controller (Sunlight Backup)

findings.label: Maximum backup load with no battery
findings.value: 30% of the IQ8 array's total rated AC output (Enphase example: 24 IQ8 = 5.7 kW AC, so backup loads under 1.7 kW AC)
findings.source_title: Enphase Sunlight Backup user guide (Essential load selection)
findings.note: Quoted: 'Enphase recommends your backup loads do not exceed 30% of the total rated AC output power.' Check: 0.30 × 5.7 kW = 1.71 kW. The page shows only a 2026 copyright date.

findings.label: What happens when loads exceed solar output
findings.value: System shuts down; takes up to 2 minutes to restart if sunlight is available
findings.note: Quoted: 'While running off-grid, the system may shutdown if the power produced is less than what is needed to power the loads' and 'The system can take up to two minutes to restart'. Enphase also says the system tries to find and disconnect the load that caused the shutdown.

findings.label: Hardware needed beyond the microinverters
findings.value: At least one IQ Load Controller, plus IQ System Controller 2 to detect the outage and switch over
findings.note: Quoted: 'Sunlight backup needs at least one IQ Load Controller installed on site'. Enphase says the IQ System Controller 2 'automatically detects utility power outages and seamlessly transitions you to backup power' and 'enables grid forming IQ8 Microinverters'.

findings.label: Batteryless outage setting and EG4's caveat
findings.value: Enable 'PV Grid Off'; EG4 says 'the Off-Grid energy is supplied by solar and is not stable'
findings.source_title: EG4 18KPV User Manual, Version 2.0.2 (ManualsLib copy), p. 50, Section 7.2 Application Settings
findings.note: Quoted: 'without installing any batteries, please enable PV Grid Off'. This is a ManualsLib copy of EG4's manual (footer: Version 2.0.2, © 2023 EG4 Electronics). I did not open EG4's own PDF.

findings.label: Solar-only backup during a grid outage
findings.value: 'No Battery' setting lets solar supply loads when the grid fails
findings.source_title: EG4 18KPV User Manual, Version 2.0.2 (ManualsLib copy), p. 84, Inverter Start-Up and Shutdown Procedure
findings.note: Quoted: "'No Battery' can be enabled to use solar power to supply load when the grid fails or load-shedding happens." The manual gives no wattage for output without a battery.

findings.label: Battery-free operation and UL listing
findings.value: Supports battery-free; 'UL 1741 by ETL for Off Grid Solar System'; 6,500 W rated, 13,000 VA peak
findings.source_title: 6.5KW 48V Split Phase Solar Inverter SPH6548P (Sun Gold Power US store)
findings.note: Read from the maker's store description with storecheck.py search. Quoted: 'a User Mode to work with all battery types, and supports battery-free.' The 13,000 VA peak figure is from the same page; the page doesn't say whether that peak is available with no battery.

findings.label: Price
findings.source_title: 6.5KW 48V Split Phase Solar Inverter SPH6548P (Sun Gold Power US store)
findings.note: From storecheck.py search of sungoldpower.com on 2026-11-13. A later product-page fetch returned HTTP 429, so the price was read once.

findings.label: Why an ordinary grid-tie inverter goes dark in an outage
findings.value: IEEE 1547 requires grid-tied inverters to detect an outage and stop exporting within 2 s (the utility can extend this to 5 s)
findings.source_title: Outagemath: Solar Without a Battery in a Power Outage: What Works
findings.note: Outagemath's summary of IEEE 1547, with the standard linked in its sources. A search excerpt from a PES GM 2026 paper quotes IEEE 1547-2018 with the same 2-second limit, but I didn't open the standard itself. This page was already in ChatGPT's results, so this point is not new.
